summary: Doctrine-disambiguation console with the operator: all 9 agenda items driven to standing decisions. 6 rows queued, 4 inline doc fixes landed, 1 item deferred to the S05 orchestration-refactor spec, 1 deferred behind T757's file hold. Two operator rulings reshape prior doctrine: (a) no single-active-orchestrator gate — any seat may register and dispatch via bin/managent unless its brief says otherwise; (b) the predictive window-budget meter is retired — agents say nothing about budget or peak hours; appetite and reactive expiring cooldowns are the only regulation, both instructions to bin/managent, never agent-maintained context.

decisions.name: who may dispatch
decisions.ruling: Any seat may register and dispatch unless its brief says otherwise: brief file first, one bin/managent registration, bin/dispatch when ready. Paste-prompts only for interactive-console targets (sessions the human must launch because no running console owns them). bin/managent + the automated dispatcher keep sprints/tasks/races conflict-free (holds/needs); no single-active-orchestrator gate. SUPERSEDES the one-ACTIVE-decider invariant of findings/T733-orcha-seat.json seed §5.

decisions.disposition: fixed inline (ROLES.md, AGENTS.md edits in this commit)

decisions.name: gate symmetry
decisions.ruling: Per-lint, not per-door: substantive lints (landmark, deliverables, edges) fire at add; display preferences (40-char title) warn everywhere, block nowhere. Covered by S05 spec ORC-REG-2 (one bundle parser for suggest/add/dispatch) + ORC-GATE-1 (seed ruling 6).
decisions.disposition: deferred to S05 — no standalone row (cross-check rule honored)

decisions.name: findings schema for queued rows
decisions.ruling: Findings files get a documented queued_kanban_rows field (array of kanban T-ids registered by the task), distinct from new_rows (CLAIMS.md proposals only). managent done accepts and validates it; refusals cite findings/README.md.
decisions.disposition: queued as T767 (this file uses the field, as the brief instructed)

decisions.name: budget meter
decisions.ruling: OVERTURNS the recalibration direction: the predictive window-budget meter is RETIRED, not recalibrated. Agents know nothing of costs and mention neither budget nor peak hours; APPETITE (steering) and temporary reactive COOLDOWN (expiring, tripped by real provider refusals) are the only regulation, both instructions to bin/managent. T736's 35M calibration is superseded (epoch-boundary note, not deletion). Spend-aware model SUGGESTION inside managent is backburner, explicitly not now. S05 spec amendment (window_budgets block + budget column out) folds into the row.

decisions.name: identifier lifecycle
decisions.ruling: Sequence written down and mechanized: assign sets model -> dispatch may launch without identifier -> claim binds identifier, DEFAULTING from the row's model -> managent agent is the manual repair verb only. unknown/<id> means genuinely unknown, never a guess (a guessed model corrupts attribution).

decisions.name: citation discipline
decisions.ruling: Affirmative rule: a brief cites committed paths; when the source is a conversation, commit a seed/findings first, then cite it (extends the T733 close gate to authoring time). Mechanism: report-only warn at add/suggest over untracked/T*.md path references (a taste gate warns, never refuses).
decisions.disposition: sentence fixed inline; mechanism queued as T764

decisions.name: one defect per name
decisions.ruling: A brief naming a defect disambiguates ID-scheme collisions from semantic collisions. Worked example recorded: 'D041/D042 binary-tag repurposing' conflated directive-ID duplication with landmark-IDs-as-area-tags (T683/T684 backfill).

decisions.name: queue cool-down semantics
decisions.ruling: Cool-down halts the AUTOMATED dispatch loop only; deliberate seat dispatches named as exceptions continue. Scoped, expiring (seed ruling 2 / ORC-PAUSE-1 carries the mechanism). Definition folded into the who-may-dispatch paragraph — one home, not two.
